absent: Numeric values, widths and byte offsets of header lengths, headroom sizes, flag offsets, pad sizes and packet size limits.
Full contract of common queue insertion, kick preparation and notification, including ordering, memory visibility and failure modes.
Locking, lifetime and teardown for queue structures, page pools, DMA mappings and scheduling contexts beyond the read side section and statistics sequencing shown.
Behavior of packet program handler, scheduler wakeup, zero copy pool management and socket buffer helpers owned elsewhere.
Negotiation of header length, queue pair count, mergeable versus large versus small modes, fragment budgets and MTU.
Complete error taxonomy and device statistics definitions beyond the down, invalid index and length error cases shown.
Layout and concurrency of shared fragment metadata, true size accounting and average length estimator.

findings.text: Device bound queue insertion for buffers already mapped for direct access. The helper requests output only handling of a single scatter description and carries the caller completion token and allocation context through to the common insertion path without performing mapping itself.

Host bound queue insertion carrying an extra caller context alongside the completion token. The helper requests input only handling of a single scatter description and forwards both opaque values and the allocation context to the common insertion path without mapping.

Wakeup entry for zero copy packet channels. It refuses work when the interface is down or the queue index is outside the current pair count, otherwise it nudges the transmit scheduler or receive scheduler or both according to direction indications and reports success.

Central receive dispatch plus refill submission. Incoming length is checked for a plausible minimum covering header and address header, direct access memory is synchronized for processor view when enabled, header flags are saved before any packet program can mutate them, and control goes to exactly one of mergeable, large packet, or small packet handling with completion only when a socket buffer results. Refill builds either a premapped single element direct description from the page address or a normal single element description, preserving caller buffer and context.

Zero copy transmit cycle. Reclaim of completed transmits runs in a mode that avoids waking packet processing, reclaimed zero copy completions are retired, a bounded batch limited by free queue slots is pulled from the transmit ring and submitted one descriptor at a time with the unsent tail completed on first failure, a single doorbell is coalesced when at least one submission succeeded, queue full handling is skipped only for raw buffer queues, transmit time is refreshed on progress, counters are accumulated under sequence protection, and the need wakeup indication is refreshed. The result signals whether any frame left.

Zero copy transmit encoding and mapping. Payload length is shifted by the flag offset constant and combined with the transmit type tag to form an opaque completion cookie. Each transmit synchronizes payload memory for device view and describes exactly two direct regions, device header followed by payload, submitted without sleeping.

Concurrency rules observed. Packet program lookup on receive uses read side critical section around dereference with unlock before returning to either program or plain path. Transmit statistics accumulation is bracketed by sequence begin and end. Transmit submission and replacement page allocation request non sleeping allocation, implying atomic or non blocking context.

Send side and device state observed through use. Send queue shows vq, sg, xsk_hdr_dma_addr, xsk_pool, napi, and stats with syncp, packets, bytes, kicks and xdp_tx. Device info shows dev, sq, rq, hdr_len, curr_queue_pairs, xdp_enabled, mergeable_rx_bufs, big_packets, big_packets_num_skbfrags, and vdev with priv pointing back. Queue shows num_free.

Receive side and header state observed through use. Receive queue shows vq, sg, page_pool, xdp_prog, xdp_rxq, use_page_pool_dma, napi, and mrg_avg_pkt_len. Mergeable header shows num_buffers plus hdr with gso_type and flags. Fragment metadata shows nr_frags, frags, xdp_frags_size and allocation warning state. Program frame shows data, data_end, data_meta, data_hard_start and frame_sz.

Headroom and program eligibility policy. Required headroom is packet program headroom when programs are enabled and none otherwise. Both small and mergeable program paths refuse segmented offload frames and partially checksummed frames before program invocation. Mergeable fast reuse additionally requires sufficient per buffer headroom and, for multi buffer frames, program support for fragments.

Coalescing and copy fallback for insufficient headroom. Coalescing allocates one replacement page, copies the first segment at a caller offset, then drains remaining mergeable segments one by one with per segment synchronization, length validation and total size guard including tail space, releasing each source page and failing with cleanup on any missing segment, bad length, oversize total, or allocation failure. The mergeable program helper uses this full coalescing when fragments are unsupported and otherwise uses a single page copy guarded by headroom plus metadata room, releasing the original in both fallback cases.

Fragment release and frame to buffer conversion. Release walks only fragment descriptors when frag metadata is present and returns each backing page to the pool. Conversion validates reserved tail room, builds a socket buffer over the frame base, carves headroom and data length from data pointers, propagates positive metadata size, and when frag metadata is present transfers fragment count, fragment size, true size and allocation warning flags.

Small packet receive behavior. Caller pad and per buffer headroom are removed to recover allocation origin, header length is subtracted and counted, overlong frames are counted as length errors, and when programs are enabled the current program if any takes the frame through a program path that rechecks headroom, initializes a program view, and on pass rebuilds lengths and optional metadata into a recyclable socket buffer while transmit or redirect verdicts produce no socket buffer here and other outcomes count program and ordinary drops with page release. Without a program the plain path copies the common header into a fresh socket buffer and marks it recyclable, dropping with page release on allocation failure.

Large packet receive behavior. Total length is validated against an allocation bound derived from configured fragment budget and page size adjusted for padded versus real header size. Valid frames are wrapped as a paged socket buffer, byte count excludes header length, and any validation or allocation failure counts a drop and returns pages to the pool.

Mergeable plain reassembly. Buffer count comes from header with processor order conversion, first segment bytes excluding header are counted after length validation, program path is taken when globally enabled and a program is installed, otherwise the first segment becomes the head socket buffer marked recyclable and each further segment is fetched, counted, optionally synchronized, validated and appended as a fragment chain with average length estimator update. Any missing segment counts a length error, any validation or append failure releases the current page, drains the remainder, counts a drop and frees the head.

Mergeable program reassembly and verdict handling. A program view is initialized over the first segment with headroom plus header excluded from data length, frag mode is enabled when more than one segment remains, total segment count beyond the fragment maximum is rejected, and each further segment is fetched, counted, synchronized when needed, validated, charged to true size and appended as a fragment descriptor with allocation warning propagation, releasing gathered frags on any failure. The verdict layer resolves the data pointer through the headroom helper, builds the frag view, invokes the handler, converts pass into a recyclable socket buffer, suppresses buffers for transmit or redirect, and on other outcomes or conversion failure releases frags and head page, drains the remainder and counts program and ordinary drops.

Untrusted peer hazards. Backend may deliver short, overlong, oversize for page, or truncated multi buffer frames and may omit segments. Short frames below header plus address header are discarded as length errors with buffer release. Overlong small frames, large frames beyond allocation, coalesced totals exceeding page including tail space, and single copies exceeding page including headroom plus metadata are dropped. Missing segments during coalescing, frag building, draining or plain append are treated as length errors with partial cleanup and drop accounting rather than use after free.
Wakeup direction indications distinguish transmit side wake from receive side wake, allowing either or both schedulers to be nudged from one call.

Program verdicts partition receive handling into pass through to stack, local transmit, redirect elsewhere, and drop or abort with drop accounting, with transmit and redirect producing no socket buffer at the receive site.
Header flag for partial checksum marks frames that program paths must drop, while header flag save and restore across program handling preserves data valid marking for frames that survive.
